title: Ramaswamy’s $4M Ad Featuring Opponent’s Estranged Mother Divides Ohio GOP
snippet: A controversial $4 million ad buy by Vivek Ramaswamy targeting Democrat Amy Acton has drawn heavy criticism from Gov. Mike DeWine, even as Donald Trump and JD Vance rally behind the aggressive tactic.
content:
A blistering $4 million campaign advertisement targeting Democratic gubernatorial nominee Dr. Amy Acton has plunged Ohio's governor race into intense personal turmoil, splintering the state's Republican establishment and sparking severe backlash over political ethics.

The commercial features Donna Arthur, Acton’s estranged biological mother, calling her daughter a "liar" and warning voters against electing her as Ohio's next governor. The ad's release, however, brought immediate scrutiny back to Acton’s tragic childhood and allegations that Arthur helped shield an abuser decades ago.

A Fractured Republican Front

The campaign spot has created a dramatic rift among high-profile conservatives. Retiring Republican Governor Mike DeWine, who previously endorsed Ramaswamy, publicly condemned the commercial on Thursday. "The ad, on its face, is deeply, deeply troubling," DeWine said, calling it outright "wrong to run." Republican Senator Jon Husted also distanced himself from the buy, indicating he would not have chosen to air such an ad.

Conversely, dominant figures on the national stage rushed to Ramaswamy’s side. Vice President JD Vance told disapproving Republicans to "stop whining" and recognize that politics is a "tough business." Meanwhile, former President Donald Trump took to Truth Social to praise Arthur's "courage," adding that Ramaswamy had "hit pay dirt."

Surfacing a History of Childhood Trauma

Acton, who gained prominence as director of the Ohio Department of Health during the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, has previously detailed her upbringing marred by neglect and abuse. Court records reveal that in 1978, Acton's stepfather was arrested and charged with raping her when she was between 9 and 12 years old. Her mother sided with the stepfather, and the couple fled Ohio to avoid trial. Acton has not spoken to her mother since testifying in court nearly 50 years ago.

Following the ad's launch, Acton’s brother issued a sharp rebuke, accusing Ramaswamy of leveraging childhood abuse as a political tool. Ramaswamy defended his campaign's decision, telling reporters that Acton’s background "deserves to be scrutinized."

Toss-Up Contest in a Shifting Political Landscape

While Ohio has trended increasingly conservative in recent election cycles—with DeWine winning reelection by more than 25 percentage points four years ago—forecasters like the Cook Political Report currently rate this year's race as a toss-up.

Acton has assembled a moderate platform focusing on affordability, police funding, and rural economic investments, giving her a competitive edge in recent polling aggregates. It remains unclear whether Ramaswamy's high-stakes $4 million ad will shift momentum in his favor or trigger voter backlash in the home stretch.
